300.author: wyhohyw
300.body:
﻿Daily CI gave RACE and FACT one shared 10-minute deadline. RACE finished, then the judge was killed while citation checking was still running, so citation accuracy and verification coverage were never recorded. On the 13 and 14 October nightlies every DRB case showed this. Forty minutes covers those runs except a DRB-64 report that cites the same manuals as dozens of distinct statements; thirty minutes still clips that report and leaves only about three minutes of margin on the next-slowest cases.

## Evaluation deadline
`.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` sets `E2E_DRB_EVAL_TIMEOUT_MS` to `2400000`. The local default stays one hour. The DeepResearchBench README's daily evaluation budget matches this deadline. Research shard jobs remain capped at 240 minutes, so the longer judge fits inside the job.

## Validation
`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. This commit changes a nightly workflow constant and its README; those layers do not execute the real DRB judge. WSL on this machine has bubblewrap, but the fresh worktree has no `node_modules`, and installing it would not observe the 40-minute deadline. The check is the next nightly after this merges and syncs to GitHub: each DRB case should record citation accuracy and verification coverage instead of `running`.

## E2E user journeys
Not applicable. No UI, API, CLI, or session behavior changes. Delivery assertions are unchanged; only the separate judge deadline in daily CI is longer.
300.head: codex/drb-eval-40m
300.title: ci: allow DRB citation scoring forty minutes

302.author: wyhohyw
302.body:
Re-running a job left the previous attempt's artifact in place. Coverage then downloaded that older package by name and failed a passed UT, because the manifest still said the first attempt failed. Closes #301.

## What changes

`actions/upload-artifact@v4` keeps an existing artifact unless `overwrite` is true. On PR #295, run 38526631198, the failed UT uploaded `ut-coverage` (`status: FAIL`, 3821/3822). The re-run passed and uploaded a second package with the same name. Coverage ran with `needs.ut.result=success` and read the 07:30 package, so `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` reported incomplete coverage.

Uploads that a later job downloads by exact name now replace the previous attempt:

- `ut-coverage`
- `st-coverage`
- `mocked-e2e-plan`
- `real-e2e-plan`

`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` fails if a workflow downloads an artifact by exact name and the matching upload omits `overwrite: true`.

## Validation

- WSL, `node --test --test-name-pattern "latest attempt" .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: 1 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. This change is GitHub Actions artifact metadata. Those layers do not observe the artifact store, and the contract test is what locks the flag.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. No product UI, API, CLI, or run path changes. The bug is which artifact a later GitHub Actions job downloads after a job re-run.
302.head: fix/ci-coverage-artifact-rerun
302.title: fix(ci): replace artifacts from a previous job attempt

303.author: zhaozhaozz
303.body:
Chat Completions responses can contain zero-filled `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` compatibility fields alongside valid `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens`. The model client preferred those aliases, so a response reporting 30,393 prompt tokens and 84 completion tokens was persisted as zero output tokens.

Use one shared usage normalizer with the actual request protocol. Chat Completions prefers prompt/completion; Responses and Anthropic prefer input/output. Aliases are fallbacks, not additional tokens. Explicit counts, including zero and counts that disagree with the reported total, are preserved; reasoning tokens are never added again. Without protocol context, a complete pair matching the total wins, including legitimate zero values. Only when neither pair matches does zero-fill recovery prefer a positive alias. Conflicting aliases retain diagnostics; when both pairs match, input/output keeps its existing precedence.

API session naming, paper vision, and evolution accounting now share the same Chat rules. Incomplete paper usage remains unknown instead of fabricating zero counts. The adapter consumes normalized internal usage events, and the metering proxy already uses the correct Chat precedence; neither needs a rule change. E2E assertions and research-delivery behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

Tested commit: `3f06f6ed76c0d6d4e97e08ef2709a1e82b1d7fa8`, based on `bb356a3f474ee6382f05420b3cf05e24d60a756e`. The follow-up adds one commit to the existing branch and changes only the shared normalizer and its unit tests; protocol-aware call sites are unchanged.

- Seven new unknown-protocol regressions all fail on the previous implementation. The complete normalization matrix now passes 19/19, including the reported `10/0/10` case, zero inputs, zero totals, matching-pair ties, and conflict diagnostics. Existing fallback tests also cover missing and inconsistent totals.
- Model typecheck: passed; the full UT layer's typecheck also passed.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 3,833 / executed 3,833 / passed 3,833, 0 failed or skipped, JiuwenSwarm backend.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 3 / executed 3 / passed 3; SDK contract sub-suite: 66 passed plus 3 subtests.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: planned 74 / executed 74 / passed 74, 0 failed or skipped; 9 additional JiuwenSwarm checks passed.
- Unmodified base `bb356a3f`: full UT planned 3,808 / executed 3,808 / passed 3,808, 0 failed or skipped, with a separate Swarm port group.

Earlier attempts encountered a dependency-download TLS failure, an incorrectly exported test dependency variable, and a parallel Swarm startup port collision. The final full UT runs used the standard environment and verified distinct bound ports. An intermediate blocked-queue assertion did not reproduce in the clean candidate or base runs. No assertion or product behavior was changed to resolve these validation issues.

## E2E user journeys

PASS at the current head — `pnpm ci:e2e` ran all 74 mocked browser journeys (research 20, standard 48, literature 6), plus the 9 Swarm checks above.

Historical targeted API evidence, tested at the first commit `c85c3cf8874a7571b47ea66e17d71209916efba1`: isolated production API and Runner CLIs with a local provider stub, using both native and JiuwenSwarm executors. Five scenarios per backend each completed a reply, queried persisted public `/usage`, and continued the same session: 20 completed Runs. Observed input/output/total tuples were `30393/84/30477`, `10/7/19`, `10/0/10`, and `8/5/13` for Responses and Anthropic; repeated cumulative frames did not increase totals. These targeted API journeys were not rerun for the unknown-protocol-only follow-up; the production callers explicitly pass their protocol and are unchanged.

The paid real-provider L3 suite was not rerun. E2E assertions and research-delivery behavior are unchanged.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

New model calls record usage according to their API dialect. No configuration or storage migration is required; historical usage records are not rewritten.
303.head: fix/api-dialect-token-usage
303.title: fix(model): prefer protocol token fields over conflicting aliases

304.author: zy95-12
304.body:
## Summary

Fix protocol-specific token usage parsing and make provider accounting non-gating in real E2E. No provider-specific workaround, Swarm source modification, or relaxation of task/delivery/quality assertions.

## Problem and evidence

The October 14 manual daily run (38546559384) completed the functional steps of seven basic journeys but failed each on `outputTokens > 0`. The preceding official-DeepSeek nightly passed the same checks.

A short Chat Completions probe returned both standard `completion_tokens: 31` and an extra `output_tokens: 0` (input 35, total 66). The shared normalizer preferred the latter. The model gateway then forwarded the incorrect zero to Swarm. No credentials or live response payloads are committed.

## Changes

- Require the requested protocol when normalizing usage. Chat Completions reads prompt/completion token fields; Responses reads input/output token fields, including its cache detail object.
- Preserve legitimate zero values. Do not reconstruct missing input/output counts from totals or fall back to another protocol's fields. Missing/invalid accounting remains unavailable and does not fail model generation.
- Remove provider token counts and usage availability as real basic-journey pass criteria. Preserve usage evidence (or an unavailable diagnostic) and the existing request ledger. Functional assertions remain unchanged; accounting does not gate scoring.
- Document this boundary. Deterministic parsing and gateway tests remain gating.

## Validation

- Model package tests: 50 passed.
- Model gateway tests: 35 passed, including streaming/non-streaming accounting propagation and completion without reported usage.
- Regression cases cover conflicting fields, null/missing/invalid values, legitimate zero, and final usage-only streaming chunks.
- Test TypeScript check (`tsconfig.tests.json`): passed.
- API dependency build: passed.
- Documentation checks: passed (126 files); `git diff --check`: passed.

The seven paid real journeys and full nightly suite have not been rerun for this PR. This fixes accounting and CI policy, not the separate evolution thinking-budget or research-team timeout failures. Token usage is provider-reported telemetry, not a guarantee of billing completeness or a reliable budget limit when the provider omits it.
304.head: fix/usage-protocol-nonblocking
304.title: fix: parse usage by protocol and keep real E2E accounting non-gating

306.author: yuanzhou75
306.body:
Nightly BiomniBench-DA currently submits the pinned original task and the platform delivery appendix without requesting the research-team workflow. Append the following instruction, verbatim, through the shared prompt builder used by both `da-13-3` and `da-14-1`:

> Make sure to use the science-research-team skill and dispatch multiple sub-agents to help me solve this task. No knowledge domain needed. No web-search needed.

The original `instruction.md` continues to be read, verified against its pinned Git blob hash, and preserved verbatim. The supplement appears once, before the existing delivery appendix. The actual submitted prompt remains available in `prompt.txt`. Daily and release runs share this entry point. Update the existing unit coverage, E2E metadata and benchmark documentation accordingly. This requests the workflow; it does not assert that the model actually invoked the skill or dispatched multiple sub-agents.

## Validation

Tested commit: `f4457b9d16aba5067c82df06879360c6bb602606`, based on upstream main `cc974a14468cbdfd66c76f2720ebd751aefb1cdd`.

- `node --experimental-strip-types --test test/benchmarks/biomnibench-da/cases.unit.ts`: 2 executed, 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Covers both task IDs, exact supplemental text and single insertion, and preservation of CRLF, Unicode and trailing whitespace in the original instruction fixture.
- `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: 62 spec files, 0 errors, 11 existing legacy warnings.
- Documentation link check: 126 Markdown files passed. Markdown lint: 127 files checked, 0 issues.
- `pnpm build`: passed during mocked E2E preparation.
- Full local `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e`: attempted on Linux/WSL with working bubblewrap, each bounded to 180 seconds plus 15 seconds termination grace. All remain **BLOCKED/incomplete**, not passes: UT stopped during JiuwenSwarm preparation (exit 124); ST stopped during build/dependency preparation (exit 137, registry download timeout in the log); mocked E2E completed build and dependency installation but stopped while installing Chromium (exit 124). No frozen plans or test summaries were produced, so planned/executed/passed counts are unavailable for these full layers. No test assertion failure was observed; no claim is made that upstream main passes these layers locally.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED** for live Biomni browser journeys at the tested SHA. The intended scenarios are DA-13-3 and DA-14-1: submit the verified original instruction plus the workflow supplement, then deliver the required artifacts and collect the existing rubric score. Neither live scenario was executed because the local terminal has no configured authorized dataset root or generator/judge credentials. The focused unit checks validate prompt construction, not real skill invocation, child-agent execution or scientific quality. Mocked browser coverage is also incomplete as described above.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal` (GitHub label pending application by a maintainer if contributor permissions prevent it).
User impact: internal benchmark input consistency for nightly and release CI.
Compatibility and migration: none.
